ai.title: Chainalysis says hackers stole credentials and tokens for all of its customers
ai.brief: Company said a “multifront cyberattack” included AI agents and an on-path data snatch. Blockchain analysis firm Chainalysis said that hackers have obtained sensitive personal information—including names, usernames, password hashes, and live tokens—for all of its users following a breach of its network security. The accomplishment could be a major coup for the attackers. Both Chainalysis and public sources have revealed a long list of high-profile customers, including government agencies such as the FBI, US Immigration and Customs Enforcement agency, and the US Air Force, as well as private companies such as Microsoft, Coinbase, and Barclays. It’s unclear if the data theft exposed customers to additional threats.

sec.title: ARTEX abuse expands as cybercriminals target financial sector
sec.brief: In this article Mitigation and protection guidance Microsoft Defender detections Hunting queries Indicators of compromise In October 2026, the financially motivated threat actor Storm-3358 began targeting organizations in the financial sector using the agentic AI offensive framework ARTEX. The threat actor that Microsoft Threat Intelligence tracks as Storm-3358 is a Cambodia-based intrusion cluster that primarily targets financial organizations in Southeast Asia, in addition to a smaller number of large financial organizations globally. Microsoft has observed Storm-3358 use ARTEX in combination with conventional automated tools to scan systems connected to the public internet, exploit security flaws including anonymous file upload and server-side request forgery (SSRF), and install open-source remote access trojans (RATs). Storm-3358 has used the WISP, vshell, and AdaptixC2 RATs for persistence and lateral movement.
